analysis:
MARKET REGIME: SPY is in a confirmed downtrend (-4.2% vs SMA50, -0.66% 20d slope). This is the single most important input today. The strategy explicitly calls for preferring cash or materially smaller size in broad downtrends. Quality-value's deepest drawdowns are market-wide, not name-specific — adding equity exposure now means fighting the tape.

PORTFOLIO REVIEW:
• ULTA (+8.06%) and UHS (+5.02%) are performing well; theses intact, hold.
• ADSK (+3.44%) grinding upward, holding above cost; thesis intact.
• NXPI (+0.70%) essentially flat but basing, still in screened candidates with improving technicals; hold.
• FOXA (+0.64%) basically flat; low-volatility position, no action needed.
• AMP (-7.70%) is the concern flag. It does NOT appear in this cycle's screened candidates — meaning it has either slipped into a downtrend or failed a quality filter. Down nearly 8% from cost in a down-market environment with financial services under pressure. This position warrants a close review: if AMP is now in a confirmed downtrend or its SMA50 slope has turned negative, the thesis may be breaking. The existing stop-loss should be respected; if not already set, a stop at approximately $465 (~8% below current, within ATR tolerance) is appropriate to protect remaining capital.

CAPACITY ANALYSIS: With 86% of equity deployed across 6 positions and only $9,185 of remaining headroom before hitting the 95% gross cap, any new position would be capped at roughly 9.4% of equity. At that size, even a 2:1 R/R trade contributes less than 1% to portfolio alpha while adding market beta in a downtrend. The math does not support forcing an entry.

SCREENED CANDIDATES: Several candidates look interesting fundamentally (TXN with +14.6% EPS revision and strong momentum; TKO with +29.1% EPS revision; DOV basing near fair value) but: (1) TXN is at 80% of 52w range and extending — borderline overextended entry; (2) TKO is MIXED/SIDEWAYS with negative SMA50 slope; (3) DOV is fine but adds industrial sector exposure with no capacity advantage. None clear the bar of 'genuinely asymmetric' given the regime headwind and position-sizing constraints.

DECISION: Zero new trades. Cash is a position. The highest-probability action is to protect the existing book, monitor AMP for stop execution, let the market regime clarify, and deploy the $9,185 headroom only when a clear Stage-1-to-Stage-2 breakout appears in a market that has stabilized. A quiet, mostly-deployed book that avoids adding beta into a downtrend is the correct posture here.
